digest.component_or_area: reconciliation bridge workflows and push core
propositions: Two YAML CAS push loops (reconcile-bridge.yml lines 272-377 and reconcile-bridge-canary.yml lines 208-246) duplicate the logic in push.py lines 161-296 with divergent implementations: YAML has 5 retries plus final push while push.py has 3 retries with missing final push

A new core entrypoint commit_and_push_tickets_branch must stage+commit only when dirty then unconditionally delegate to push, preserving the reconciler's precommitted binding-store state and handling both clean and dirty worktrees correctly

Strict delivery mode must raise a dedicated catchable PushDeliveryError carrying git reason and unpushed-commit count on ALL silent returns (non-retriable decline, merge-recovery guard, store-epoch guard, final-push rejection, lock timeout, and sync.push contradiction), with only the private module CLI translating to stderr and non-zero exit

Both workflows must invoke named actions through python -m rebar._store.push (commit-and-push --strict for reconciler, push --strict for canary) with REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always pinned, and contain zero raw git writes

The five merge/retry cycle budget applies uniformly to both strict and best-effort callers; strict is opt-in at call sites and existing best-effort callers inherit only the durability fix without disposition change

Commit authorship must be passed explicitly to the core entrypoint via author_name and author_email parameters, applied per-commit via git -c config options, falling back to ambient identity when unset
